title: Process: new user-facing commands ship with an MCP tool (or a filed follow-up)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**Proposal (for the owner to accept or decline):** a new user-facing command ships with an MCP tool, or with a filed follow-up issue.

**Why:** the MCP server (#128) lets an agent drive CamCraft headlessly: import, stock, tools, operations, generate, verify, post. Each GUI feature that lands without an MCP tool widens the gap. #348 just added tool-library import/export to the GUI only, which is now a follow-up issue (see the linked issue). The existing gaps are #180 (picking faces, edges and loops), #181 (work offsets, the machine, fixtures), #182 (sim render) and #312 (hole detection for drilling).

The cost is usually small. Per the #128 decisions, the MCP tools call the same undoable commands the GUI uses, so wiring one in is mostly a schema plus a handler in `crates/app/src/mcp/`.

**Possible rule text for AGENTS.md ("Everything Is a Command" section):**
> A PR that adds a user-facing command also adds its MCP tool (and script verb where it fits), or files a `source:agent` follow-up issue "MCP: <command>" and names it in the PR body.

**Possibly also:** a project skill, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/`, describing the agent workflow and its known gaps:
- the workflow: open/import → set_stock → add_tool → add_operation → generate → verify → post;
- the param DTO shapes;
- refusals as data;
- the known gaps (machine and work offset not settable, no hole detection).

A contributor driving a job end to end over MCP (a simple plate on a Tormach 770MX, verified and run clean in PathPilot Hub) had to work these gaps out by hand.

Filed from a contributor session. Not claimed: this is a process decision for the owner.
